record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: For every pair of real numbers α and β, is liminf_{q→∞} q⟨qα⟩⟨qβ⟩ equal to 0, where ⟨x⟩ denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 38 (Littlewood). For any α, β ∈ R, lim inf q→∞ q 〈qα〉 〈qβ〉= 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real number $x$, let $\langle x\rangle := \min_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} |x-n|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Determine whether, for every pair of real numbers $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$\liminf_{q\to\infty}\; q\,\langle q\alpha\rangle\,\langle q\beta\rangle \;=\; 0,$$
where the limit inferior is taken over positive integers $q$.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is the classical Littlewood conjecture (circa 1930), which remains open in general. The strongest known partial result is due to Einsiedler, Katok, and Lindenstrauss (Annals of Math., 2006), which shows that the set of exceptional pairs $(\alpha,\beta)$ for which the equality fails has Hausdorff dimension zero. No proof or disproof of the full conjecture is known.

status_evidence.title: Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Einsiedler, Katok, Lindenstrauss prove that the set of pairs (α,β) not satisfying Littlewood's conjecture has Hausdorff dimension zero.
status_evidence.claim: Best known partial result; full conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Littlewood conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture, posed by John Edensor Littlewood around 1930, remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The Littlewood conjecture is still open as of current literature.
